sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily, I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Nicaragua.
Nicaragua is a warm, green and friendly country
in Central America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Nicaragua?
Nicaragua is in Central America.
It is between Honduras and Costa Rica.
It has coasts on the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
It has volcanoes, lakes and rainforests.
What is the capital city of Nicaragua?
The capital city is Managua.
Managua is the largest city in the country.
It has museums, markets, parks and lakes.
Other cities include Leon, a city with history and churches.
Granada, colorful with colonial buildings.
Messiah, famous for crafts and volcano views.
Bluefields on the Caribbean coast.
How many people live in Nicaragua?
About six, eight million people live in Nicaragua.
Most people live in the West near the Pacific side.
Many live in small towns or countryside villages.
What language do people speak in Nicaragua?
The official language is Spanish.
In the Caribbean region, people also speak English Creole.
Some indigenous groups speak mosquito,
Garifuna and other native languages.
What is the weather like in Nicaragua?
Nicaragua has a tropical climate.
Dry season from November to April.
Rainy season from May to October.
It is usually hot and humid, but cooler in the mountains.
What does Nicaragua look like?
Nicaragua has lakes like Nicaragua, the largest in Central America.
Volcanoes, some are active.
Forests, mountains and rivers.
Beautiful beaches on both the Pacific and Caribbean sides.
It is called the land of lakes and volcanoes.
What animals live in Nicaragua?
Nicaragua has many animals such as monkeys, jaguars and deer,
toucans, parrots and eagles, crocodiles, iguanas and frogs,
turtles and fish in the ocean and lakes.
You can see many animals in nature reserves.
What do people eat in Nicaragua?
Nicaragua food is simple, tasty and often made with corn and rice.
People eat rice and beans, often together as gallopinto,
tortillas, plantains and cheese, chicken, pork and fish.
Fruits like mango, papaya and pineapple.
Popular dishes, nicotamal.
Corn dough with meat, steamed in banana leaves.
Indio via hoe meets stew with onions and corn.
Frittanga, grilled meat with rice, plantains and salad.
What do people drink in Nicaragua?
People drink water.
Fresh fruit juice like hibiscus or passion fruit.
Coffee, Nicaragua grows very good coffee,
chicha, a sweet drink made from corn.
Adults may drink rum or local beer.
In hot weather, cold drinks are popular.
What is life like in Nicaragua?
Life in Nicaragua is family-centered, simple and active.
People enjoy spending time with family and neighbors,
listening to music and dancing,
going to church, playing baseball and football,
visiting nature and lakes.
In villages, life is calm and full of tradition.
What are some holidays and traditions in Nicaragua?
Independence Day, September 15th,
Holy Week, Samana Santa, with processions and prayers.
Christmas with lights, food and music.
La Griteria, a Catholic celebration in December.
Patrons Saint Festivals in many towns.
People celebrate with parades, fireworks and traditional dance.
Some fun facts about Nicaragua.
Lake Nicaragua has freshwater sharks.
It has over 20 volcanoes, and some you can climb.
The Nicaraguan flag is blue and white,
with a triangle in the center.
Baseball is more popular than football.
Nicaragua has many colorful buses called chicken buses.
Now you know many things about Nicaragua.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the lakes, the food and the festivals.
Well done.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Spanish, Adios.
